settingsDialog.title: Settings
settingsDialog.showExtraKpisHint: Controls the "Additional KPIs" section on the Sprint Report card - when off, it's hidden on screen and left out of every emailed/exported report (HTML, PDF, PPTX). Saved in this browser.

azdoPatSteps.step1: In Azure DevOps, open your profile (top right) and go to User Settings > Personal Access Tokens.
azdoPatSteps.step2: Click "New Token", give it a name, and set scopes to Work Items (Read) and Test Plans (Read).
azdoPatSteps.step3: Click "Create" and copy the token right away - Azure DevOps only shows it once.
azdoPatSteps.step4: In the dashboard, click "Change PAT" (or use the first-run screen) and paste your organization name plus PAT.
azdoPatSteps.step5: The values stay only in this browser's local storage and are sent only to your local dashboard process.

kpisHelp.totalTestCases: All test cases in the selected plan(s), regardless of their status.
kpisHelp.executedCount: Cases with outcome Passed, Failed, or Blocked. Any other outcome (Not Applicable, Not Run, Paused, In Progress) isn't counted as executed here - unlike each suite's own "% Executed" badge further down, which counts Not Applicable as executed too.
kpisHelp.notApplicable: Cases marked Not Applicable (N/A), i.e. not relevant for this sprint.
kpisHelp.notRun: Cases not yet executed: Total minus Executed minus N/A. This also folds in any Paused or In Progress cases, since only Passed/Failed/Blocked count as "executed" above.
kpisHelp.passedCount: Number of test cases with a Passed outcome, with its share of all test cases. This is the numerator of the Pass Rate (which instead uses only the usable cases, Total minus N/A, as its base).
kpisHelp.passRate: Percentage of Passed cases over the total usable cases (Total minus N/A). N/A cases are excluded.
kpisHelp.effectiveBugsDetected: Valid bugs found, excluding out-of-scope ones (duplicates, not relevant, etc.) - shown as effective bugs out of the total detected.
kpisHelp.outOfScopeBugsDetected: Bugs found but excluded from the main count because they're out of scope (duplicates, not reproducible, not relevant).
kpisHelp.bugsByUs: Bugs found by our test team: every detected bug (including out-of-scope ones) whose source is neither DSI nor Test Business.
kpisHelp.bugsByDsi: Bugs reported directly by DSI: every detected bug (including out-of-scope ones) linked to the DSI source.
kpisHelp.bugsByBusiness: Bugs with suite "Test Business": every detected bug (including out-of-scope ones) whose origin is business testing. Shown even when it's 0.
kpisHelp.bugsClosedRatio: Percentage of Closed bugs over the total bugs found (Closed divided by Total), including any out-of-scope bugs that were closed.
kpisHelp.bugsToClose: Bugs not yet Closed over the total bugs found (Total minus Closed), including any out-of-scope bugs not yet closed.
kpisHelp.criticalBugs: Critical-severity bugs that are still open, counted only among in-scope (effective) bugs - unlike the other bug counts on this card, out-of-scope bugs are excluded here.
kpisHelp.reopenedBugs: Bugs that have been reopened at least once after being closed, based on their full history - regardless of current status, and counted across every detected bug including out-of-scope ones.
kpisHelp.avgClosureTime: Average number of days between a bug being opened and closed, across every detected bug (including out-of-scope ones) that has an actual closed date. Bugs still open aren't counted yet.
kpisHelp.withoutResolutionDate: Bugs still active (not Closed, Da verificare, or In verifica) that don't have an estimated resolution date set yet. A separate figure from the closure-time average above, which is based on each bug's actual closed date.
kpisHelp.firstExecutionPassRateFunctional: % of Functional-plan test cases that passed on their very first execution attempt (not the current/latest outcome). Target >= 80%.
kpisHelp.firstExecutionPassRateUat: % of UAT-plan test cases that passed on their very first execution attempt (not the current/latest outcome). Target >= 90%.
kpisHelp.avgFixTimeBusinessDays: Average business days (Mon-Fri) between a bug being opened and its first transition into Resolved/Da verificare (fix ready for retest) - not calendar days to Closed. Target <= 2 business days.
kpisHelp.criticalHighBugPct: Open bugs at Critical or High severity, as a percentage of total detected bugs. Target <= 0.5%.
kpisHelp.testPlanCorrectnessPct: % of planned test cases not Blocked by a linked bug. Note: a test case marked Blocked with no linked bug does not currently reduce this score - QA must link a bug to a Blocked case for it to count here. Target 95-100%.
kpisHelp.duplicateNotApplicable: Not Applicable test cases whose title also appears as Not Applicable in another suite of the selected plan(s), or in the previous sprint's plan(s). Matched by title, not ID, since a re-added test case gets a new work item ID. Target 0.

sectionHelp.suiteProgress: Each suite's own "% Executed" counts Not Applicable as executed too (only Not Run is excluded) - broader than the "Test Cases Executed" KPI above, which excludes Not Applicable entirely. Pass Rate = Passed Ã· (Total minus Not Applicable).
sectionHelp.bugStatus: Every bug detected for this sprint/area, including out-of-scope ones, grouped by current Azure DevOps status. "Still open" counts only in-scope (effective) bugs not yet Closed - narrower than the totals above it.
sectionHelp.originBreakdown: "Detected" counts every bug attributed to this source, including out-of-scope ones. "Accepted" counts only the in-scope (effective) bugs from that same source. A bug's source is Test Factory by default, unless its linked suite identifies it as Test Agenti, Business, or DSI (DSI bugs are counted in the KPI tile above, not shown as their own panel here).

guide.title: Excel Report Guide
guide.generatedWith: Report generated by the QA dashboard from Azure DevOps.
guide.how: Data is read live from the Azure DevOps REST APIs at generation time: the bug list from the selected sprint and area path, test execution and test cases from the selected plans. The server caches results for 5 minutes; the "Refresh data" button forces a re-read. Rows are never truncated in the downloaded file (they are in the on-screen preview).
guide.multiScopeNote: Combined report across several scopes: every list sheet has a filterable "Scope" column and the Summary shows one column per scope plus the Total.
guide.summaryWhat: Aggregated sprint KPIs: test execution, bugs by status / severity / origin, DSI overview. In the combined report one column per scope + Total (Total percentages are recomputed from summed numerator/denominator, not averaged).
guide.bugsWhat: Every in-scope sprint bug, deduplicated, one row per bug. Also includes bugs not linked to any test case (DSI, business, tagged only by area path).
guide.bugsSource: sprintDefectReport.effectiveDefects (server-side match on iteration + area path).
guide.bugsBySuiteWhat: Only bugs linked to a test case that lives in a suite of the selected plans. One row per bug-suite pair (a bug in two suites appears twice). A subset of "Sprint Bugs".
guide.bugsBySuiteSource: planOverview.suites[].bugs; severity is looked up from effectiveDefects.
guide.todaysBugsWhat: Detected bugs (any origin, in or out of scope) created or changed today in the report timezone.
guide.todaysBugsSource: sprintDefectReport.todaysDefects (pre-filtered and sorted by the server, newest activity first).
guide.dsiWhat: Every bug whose suite (Custom.Suite field) is "Test DSI", with its description. Independent of the selected plans.
guide.businessWhat: Every bug reported by Test Business (Custom.Suite = "Test Business"), with its description. Open ones sorted first; filterable "Open" column. Independent of the selected plans.
guide.suitesWhat: One row per suite of the selected plans: outcome counts, % executed, % pass, open bugs.
guide.testCasesWhat: One row per test case of the selected plans with execution outcome, who ran it, assigned tester, configuration, tags, test case state, automation, linked bugs and more.
guide.testCasesSource: planOverview.testCases: built from the test points (outcome, last run, runner, configuration) and the test case work item (state, tags, assignee, automation).
guide.plansWhat: One row per selected test plan: suite count, total tests, executed, % executed, % pass, bug count.
guide.assigneesWhat: Bug count per assignee for the sprint.
guide.legendOutcome:
Passed / Failed / Blocked = a verdict was reached (counts as "executed").
NotApplicable = case not applicable to this sprint.
Paused / InProgress = execution started but not finished.
NotRun = never executed.
When a case has several test points the shown outcome is the aggregate: Failed wins, then Blocked, Paused, InProgress; "all Passed" = Passed.
guide.legendFlags:
Executed = outcome is Passed, Failed or Blocked.
Not run = outcome is NotRun.
Needs retest = executed but has open linked bugs: re-run it after the fix.
guide.legendColors:
Severity: 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4+ grey.
Percentages: green ok, yellow warning, red critical (green/red inverted where "lower is better", e.g. % DSI of total).
Bug status: green Closed, blue/teal in verification, orange in progress, red New, pink Reopened.
guide.legendCalcTitle: How the main indicators are computed
guide.legendCalc:
% Executed = (Passed+Failed+Blocked) / total tests.
% Pass = Passed / (total tests - NotApplicable).
Open bugs = total bugs - Closed bugs.
Critical bugs open = non-Closed bugs with severity "1 -".
Mean time to resolution (MTTR) = average days between creation and closure of closed bugs.
Days since last run = from today to the test case's last run date.
